elizajs.js and eliza-script.js in this directory are vendored from:

  https://github.com/urbanautomaton/eliza-js
  commit a2e64737137398c138b3a26b0f96078ae835f49b (master, 2014-01-06), fetched 2026-09-23

(Landsteiner's older "elizabot.js" was considered first, but its own page only
says the code is "free software and provided 'as is'" with no explicit
permission grant, and its npm package lists no SPDX license -- ambiguous, so
a different, clearly-licensed implementation was used instead, per the "stop
and report if a license is unclear; pick another" instruction.)

elizajs.js bundles the upstream lib/eliza/{decomp,key,linked_list,
ordered_hash,responder,eliza}.js files verbatim into one browser-loadable
file behind a tiny local CommonJS-style shim (no bundler, no network access);
no logic was changed. eliza-script.js is the upstream lib/eliza/script.js
data file (Coffey's JSON-style translation of Weizenbaum's original 1966
DOCTOR script), reproduced verbatim except that its last line
("module.exports = script;", referring to an undefined variable -- the
object is actually named eliza_script) was replaced with a working
UMD-ish export, since that line would throw if it were ever actually
required upstream. See the header comments in each file for details.

The underlying ELIZA/DOCTOR concept and dialogue style originate with
Joseph Weizenbaum's 1966 program and are in the public domain; only this
particular JS implementation and script encoding are Simon Coffey's
copyrighted, MIT-licensed work.
